name: WPI FIRST Robotics Scholarship
deadline: Applications typically open mid-December and close in late February
notes: For FIRST Robotics Competition, FIRST Tech Challenge, or FIRST Global Challenge team members admitted to WPI. One of the largest scholarships available to FIRST alumni.

name: Rose-Hulman FIRST Robotics Scholarship
deadline: Typically due February 1 — must already be admitted to apply
notes: Two awarded per year to admitted students who competed on a FIRST Robotics Competition team, contingent on maintaining good academic standing.

name: Kettering University Robotics Scholarship
amount: Up to $5,000/year, up to $25,000 over 5 years
deadline: Application window typically opens November 1; accepted students apply by March 1
notes: Kettering has awarded nearly $5 million in robotics scholarships since 1999 — up to 50 awarded annually to FRC/VEX competitors.

name: Michigan Tech FIRST Scholarship
deadline: Awarded competitively to incoming first-year applicants — apply as part of admission
notes: Open to incoming students who competed on a FIRST Robotics Competition, FIRST Tech Challenge, or VEX Robotics team.

name: FIRST Scholarship Program
amount: Up to $4,000/year, renewable up to 4 years
deadline: Check current cycle on Detroit Mercy's site
notes: For high school seniors with a background in robotics, including FIRST Robotics Competition participants.

name: FIRST Scholars Award
deadline: Check current cycle on Mercer's site
notes: Awarded to admitted students selected as Mercer FIRST Scholars based on their FIRST program participation.

name: FIRST/VEX Robotics Engineering Scholarship
deadline: Check current cycle on Oregon Tech's site
notes: Two awarded per year. Requires two years of active participation and demonstrated leadership on a FIRST Robotics Competition, FIRST Tech Challenge, or VEX team.

name: FIRST Robotics Scholarship
deadline: Check current cycle on Georgia Tech's site
notes: Offered to graduating high school seniors admitted to Georgia Tech who participated in FIRST Robotics Competition.

name: Elbit America FIRST Robotics Scholarship (New Hampshire)
deadline: Check current cycle on Elbit America's application portal
notes: Restricted to New Hampshire high school seniors who competed on a FIRST Robotics Competition team.

name: Stamps President's Scholars Program
amount: Full ride — tuition, fees, room & board, books, and personal expenses for up to 4 years
deadline: Tied to Georgia Tech's Early Action admission deadline; semifinalists notified in January, finalists invited to Scholars Weekend in late February
notes: Open to US and UK high school seniors applying for admission to Georgia Tech. About 50 awarded per year through a multi-round process including a semifinalist interview and a finalist weekend; no separate application beyond Georgia Tech admission.

name: Regents' and Chancellor's Scholarship
amount: $2,500/year honorary award for scholars without demonstrated need; scholars with need receive funding up to their full calculated need
deadline: No separate application — tied to the UC application (due in November); interviews in early March, decisions by late March
notes: Awarded to incoming first-years and some transfers based on academic achievement, leadership, and service shown on the UC application; renewable for up to 8 semesters.

name: Engineering Scholarship of Honor
provider: University of Michigan College of Engineering
amount: $10,000/year for in-state students; $10,000–$30,000/year for out-of-state students, renewable up to 8 semesters
deadline: No separate application — automatic consideration upon admission, with award notification typically by mid-April
notes: All admitted US citizens and permanent residents entering the College of Engineering are automatically considered based on their admissions application.

name: Trustees Scholarship
amount: $10,000/year for Indiana residents; $16,000/year for non-residents, renewable up to 4 years with a 3.00 Purdue GPA
deadline: November 1 — no separate application; automatic merit review of the admission application
notes: Awarded to incoming first-year applicants for exceptional academic achievement plus leadership or service in school or community.

name: President's Endowed Scholarship
amount: $3,000/year for 4 years ($12,000 total), plus a one-time $1,000 study-abroad award; renewable with a 3.5 cumulative GPA
deadline: December 1 — covered by the same admission/scholarship application (ApplyTexas or Common App)
notes: Merit-based award for entering first-time freshmen in the top 25% of their graduating class; no separate scholarship application required.

name: Barry M. Goldwater Scholarship
deadline: National deadline is the last Friday in January; each college sets its own earlier internal nomination deadline, often November–December
notes: For current college sophomores and juniors (3.0+ GPA, US citizen, national, or permanent resident) pursuing a research career in natural sciences, mathematics, or engineering. Requires nomination by your institution — students cannot apply directly.

name: SWE Scholarship Program
amount: Individual awards generally $1,000–$10,000, varying by named award within the program
deadline: Varies by track — Collegiate/Graduate Scholars and Emerging First-Year Scholars tracks typically close in late winter/early spring
notes: Open to women entering or enrolled in an ABET-accredited undergraduate or graduate engineering, engineering technology, or computer science program. One application considers a student for all eligible society-level awards.

name: NSBE Scholarships
deadline: Varies by cycle — multiple cycles run per year; check current dates on NSBE's site
notes: Requires active, paid NSBE membership and a verified GPA on file. Specific major, classification, and residency requirements vary by individual sponsored award.

name: AISES Scholarships
provider: American Indian Science and Engineering Society
deadline: Applications generally open mid-December and close April 30 each cycle
notes: Requires free AISES student membership and full-time enrollment in a STEM field at an accredited institution. A single profile in AISES's OASIS portal matches students to eligible named scholarships.

name: Regeneron Science Talent Search
amount: Top 300 scholars each receive $2,000 (plus $2,000 to their school); 40 finalists receive at least $25,000, with top awards up to $250,000
deadline: Early November — check current cycle on site
notes: Open to students in their final year of secondary school in the US or its territories, including US citizens studying abroad, based on an original, independent research project. Team research is not eligible.

name: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
amount: $10,000, $25,000, or $50,000 tiers in most categories, with top STEM/math fellows eligible for $100,000 (exact tiers can vary slightly by year)
deadline: Mid-February — check current cycle on site
notes: Open to students 18 or younger who have completed a significant, original piece of work in STEM, technology, engineering, math, or other fields. Individuals or 2-person teams are eligible.

name: SME Education Foundation Scholarships
deadline: Varies by program — most open in fall/winter
notes: Not FIRST-exclusive, but manufacturing/engineering-focused scholarships that many FRC alumni are well-positioned for given hands-on robotics experience.

name: Robotics Education Scholarship
deadline: Check current cycle on NFPA's site
notes: For a high school senior who participated in FIRST, VEX, or the National Robotics League.
